office_does: A State Representative writes and votes on Washington state law and the operating, capital and transportation budgets, covering school funding, tax structure, housing rules, health funding and criminal-justice statutes.
race_blurb: Democratic incumbent Brandy Donaghy, Vice Chair of House Transportation since her 2021 appointment, faces first-time Republican candidate Chris Elder; both are Navy veterans. Donaghy voted for the 2025 and 2026 tax increases; Elder runs on cutting wasteful spending rather than raising taxes.

candidates.summary: Incumbent State Representative since 2021 and House Transportation vice chair, a Navy veteran whose record centers road safety, emergency preparedness and consumer protection.
highlights: Sponsored traffic safety camera expansion (2024), young-driver education (2025) and school albuterol access (2026) [S3]
States that reproductive health care and gender-affirming care are health care [S2]
Voted for the 2026 tax on income over $1 million and the 2025 tax increases [S7][S8][S9][S10]
Voted for EHB 1217 (2025 rent-increase limits) and ESHB 1296 (2025 parents' rights amendments) [S11][S12]

taxes.basis: Voted for ESSB 6346 (9.9% tax on income over $1 million) and for the 2025 capital gains/estate, excise and B&O tax increases.

spending.basis: Supports public investment in affordable childcare, healthcare-workforce pipelines and behavioral-health and crisis-response funding; no spending-restraint positions.

housing.basis: Voted for the 2025 limits on rent and fee increases; her own housing statement emphasizes building supply through transit-oriented and co-housing models.

safety.basis: Session update frames public safety around 'prevention, early intervention' and behavioral-health and crisis-response funding.

climate.basis: Committed to policies that 'reduce carbon emissions, promote renewable and clean energy sources'; no stated position on carbon pricing.

experience.basis: Five-year incumbent and committee vice chair; opponent is a first-time candidate.

social.basis: States 'Reproductive health care is health care' and 'Gender affirming care is healthcare'; endorsed by Planned Parenthood Alliance Advocates.

parental-rights.basis: Voted for ESHB 1296, which amended the I-2081 list of parent and guardian rights; no campaign statement on the topic.

candidates.summary: First-time Republican candidate, a 20-year Navy aviation veteran, farmer, realtor and small-business owner running on spending restraint, lower taxes and public safety.
highlights: Will 'reduce wasteful spending rather than raise taxes,' citing state budget growth of more than 110% in a decade [S3]
Would 'lessen regulations that hinder affordable housing' [S3]
Supports law enforcement, more police per capita and crime prevention [S3]

taxes.basis: Pamphlet pledges to 'lower taxes'; website says he will fight to reduce spending 'rather than raise taxes' and let residents keep more of their earnings.

spending.basis: Centers his campaign on budget growth outpacing inflation, cutting waste and full spending transparency.

housing.basis: Would 'lessen regulations that hinder affordable housing'; no further housing proposals.

safety.basis: Supports law enforcement and raising Washington's low police-per-capita levels, alongside unspecified crime-prevention strategies.

experience.basis: First time seeking office, running against a five-year incumbent.
